Rhodes template constraints: 'your CV should not exceed 2 pages and no additional pages will be read by selectors'; each section carries its own space limit, so select the highest-impact experiences rather than listing all; paid work goes under section 1 and unpaid under section 2; publications must give author names, title and dates but MUST NOT include abstracts; an ORCiD may be included; completed CV is uploaded to the Embark application

FUNDER_TEMPLATE is a per-funder SCHEMA and a per-funder MECHANISM, not a stylesheet. All three verified templates differ in both: SISGP is a styled DOCX with fixed headings where deletion is allowed and any addition makes the application ineligible; Rhodes is numbered prose sections with per-section space limits and NO education section; Australia Awards is a DOCX of Word FORMTEXT form fields inside tables, with split DD/MM/YYYY date controls and a computed 'total duration in months'. Field sets are near-disjoint - duty station, medium of instruction, institution type, supervision headcount, ORCiD and network/civil-society engagement each appear at exactly one funder. Build one mapping module per funder; do not parameterise a single renderer by a heading list
Source URL [provenance]: SISGP + Rhodes + Australia Awards templates, all three downloaded and read 2026-08-21

Rule: University of Cambridge supporting documents (all postgraduate applicants, Gates Cambridge included): must be 'pdf format', 'under 2MB', and 'not encrypted'. The 2 MB ceiling is stricter than most portals and applies to the CV like any other supporting document

Filling a funder template can mean writing into a form, not rendering a page: the Australia Awards CV template is a DOCX containing legacy Word FORMTEXT form fields laid out in tables, so producing it means populating named form fields in the supplied file, not generating a PDF from our own layout. Any funder_template implementation must first determine which of the three mechanisms applies (styled headings / prose sections / fillable form fields)

Europass DOES have a summary field: the current editor carries an 'About Me' section - 'Make sure you update the About Me section to highlight why you are the best person for the job. Do not include a full detailed history. Focus on facts and main points.' Support it in the EUROPASS render variant as an OPTIONAL short block. Note the wording is employment-framed throughout (vacancy notice, best person for the job) because Europass is an EU labour-mobility tool; for an admissions CV keep it factual and short rather than a pitch

Graduate-admissions guidance routes objectives and motivation to the STATEMENT OF PURPOSE, not to the CV. Cornell: the academic statement of purpose is where the committee learns 'your academic objectives'; the personal statement covers 'how your background and experiences have influenced your decision to pursue a graduate degree'. Berkeley's admissions resume specification lists education, professional work history, professional activities, professional productivity and other activities - with no summary or profile section. Default to omitting a summary outside the Europass variant

'Include a well-written job objective' is EMPLOYMENT advice and does not transfer to admissions. The instruction appears on Cornell Graduate School's career/professional-development resume page, aimed at job seekers, and names 'the type of position and work setting you are seeking'. Admissions CVs have no vacancy to target and the applicant also submits a motivation letter or SOP, so a career objective duplicates that document in weaker, unevidenced form. Same non-transfer class as R-054 (one-page cap) and R-055 (ATS optimisation)

University of Cambridge postgraduate: AI use is PROHIBITED for the CV. Verbatim: 'AI must not be used when writing personal statements and CVs. This prohibition covers the use of AI to help your use of English.' Hallucinated achievements are treated as fraud: 'if these are about your personal achievements they will be treated like any other application fraud'. Note the prohibition explicitly extends to language polishing, so even an editing-only pass is disallowed. ai_use_policy = prohibited

Cambridge's prohibition differs BY DOCUMENT TYPE within one institution: CVs and personal statements are prohibited, while 'Appropriate use of AI tools to support the preparation of research proposals is permitted. Content generated by AI should be acknowledged.' Interviews: 'AI must not be used to impersonate or assist you during an interview... you should expect to be asked to confirm that you are not using AI.' Therefore ai_use_policy cannot be a single per-programme value - it must resolve per document kind

Gates Cambridge inherits Cambridge's prohibition. R-018 established that Gates applicants apply through the University's Graduate Application Portal and that the CV requirement comes from the University's own application - so R-087 binds Gates Cambridge applicants even though the Gates pages publish no AI policy of their own. No Gates-specific AI wording was located
Verified for cycle: current; inherited rather than separately published

Rule: University of Oxford graduate: AI may be used to RESEARCH but not to GENERATE. Verbatim: 'Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools may be used to research materials in preparing your application, but may not be used to generate documents or form the basis of documents that are then adapted.' Plagiarism policy adds: 'any submitted documents must be written by the candidate'. Consequence: 'If academic assessors consider that inappropriate use of AI was made in application documents, they may reject your application.' Generating a CV for an Oxford application is therefore disallowed; ai_use_policy = prohibited for generation

Chevening: 'Using artificial intelligence software to generate answers to Chevening's essay questions is strictly prohibited. Applicants must submit their own original work.' Enforcement is active, not nominal: 'Chevening uses tools to detect fraud, plagiarism, and AI-generated content in applications', and a fraudulent or copied application 'will be disqualified'. Scope is the essay questions; Chevening collects no CV (R-015), so this binds the motivation/essay engine rather than the CV engine

Disclosure form, where required, is a NEGATIVE ATTESTATION on the application form rather than a note in the document. Chevening: 'You will be asked to confirm that you have not used artificial intelligence to generate your answers as part of the application form.' Cambridge uses the same shape at interview: 'you should expect to be asked to confirm that you are not using AI.' A platform whose output required such a confirmation to be false would be inducing the applicant into a false declaration - the reason ai_use_policy must gate generation rather than annotate it
Binding or advisory: binding where the destination requires it
